commit.message:
feat: Kafka token invalidation feed and role-or-scope route policy

requireAny(roles, scopes) answers 403 when a valid token has neither;
AuthContext exposes roles and iat.

Every node follows the token service's invalidation topic into a local
store (app.revocation.kafka): per-jti and subject-wide invalidations
(every token a subject was issued before a cut-off, for role changes and
sign-out-everywhere). Each node reads all partitions with no consumer
group, replays max-token-lifetime on start, stays not ready until caught
up, fails closed past max-staleness, skips malformed records and never
auto-creates the topic. CI runs KafkaInvalidationsSpec against an
apache/kafka service.

Invalidate only the tokens of users whose permissions change

A PATCH on a user carries its roles, rewriting each role's name with its
own value; any save touching a role or an authorization then incremented
every user's refreshTokenVersion. The invalidator now collects, before
the save, the users whose roles or whose roles' authorizations actually
change, comparing the pending changes against the store, and increments
only theirs after it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
fix: invalidate employee session on role change, fix stale role in auth context

- EmployeeAuthMiddleware set ctx "role" from claims.Role (the JWT's
  role at login time) instead of employee.Role (the fresh DB row it
  had already fetched right above to check token_version/is_active)
  — a role change by an admin had no effect on that employee's
  authorization until their access token expired or they refreshed
- UpdateEmployee now revokes refresh tokens + bumps token_version
  when role actually changes, mirroring the invalidation pattern
  ChangePassword already uses — only fires on a role diff, not on
  every profile edit, so renaming/re-numbering an employee doesn't
  force a re-login
- existing (pre-update) employee row is now fetched unconditionally
  instead of only when req.Role == "outlet_admin", since it's now
  needed for the role-diff comparison too

[T-110] Invalidate sessions immediately when a user's role changes

Role updates previously only reassigned UserRoles, while TokenVersion bumps
and refresh-token cleanup ran only on deactivation. A demoted Admin could
keep passing Authorize(Roles=...) until the access token expired.

On a real role change, bump TokenVersion, delete refresh tokens, and clear
the token-version cache (plus close live SignalR connections) so old JWTs
fail OnTokenValidated right away.

T-0005: Invalidate token cache when a user's role/enabled changes

The user reported: after an admin changes my role, the change
isn't visible until I log out and back in. The cause is the
in-memory tokenCache (and the Redis one when REDIS_ENABLED=true)
that getCurrentUser checks on every request: it cached the user
row including the role, with a 5-minute TTL, so changes to
users.role weren't visible until the cache entry expired.

The old UpdateUser handler invalidated only the current
request's token (the admin's own), leaving every other active
session for the target user stale.

Fix: extend tokenCacheStore with DeleteByUserID(userID) and
call it from UpdateUser and SetUserEnabled so the target user's
every active session is invalidated at once.

Implementation:
  - handlers/auth.go: tokenCacheStore interface gains
    DeleteByUserID(userID string) int. The in-memory
    implementation uses sync.Map.Range to walk every entry and
    delete the ones whose user.ID matches. The Redis
    implementation calls a new utils.RedisTokenCache.ScanUserTokens
    (SCAN with the "token:" prefix, decode each value, collect
    matching tokens, then Delete each one) and falls back to a
    no-op on Redis errors so a transient cache outage doesn't
    break role changes.
  - utils/redis.go: new ScanUserTokens method that walks Redis
    with SCAN/GET, returns the underlying token strings (without
    the "token:" prefix) for the matching user.
  - handlers/auth_user_handlers.go: UpdateUser replaces the
    single-token cache delete with
    tokenCache.DeleteByUserID(req.TargetUserID), and SetUserEnabled
    adds the same call.

New tests:
  - handlers/auth_cache_test.go: TestMemoryTokenCacheDeleteByUserID
    inserts alice/bob entries, deletes alice's, asserts only
    bob's survive; checks that empty userID is a no-op.
  - handlers_user_test.go: new subtest
    "updating a role invalidates the target user's cached token so
    they see the change on next request" — primes the cache with
    member1=MEMBER, has admin promote them to ADMIN, asserts the
    member1 cache entry is gone, then issues a /auth/me with
    member1's token and verifies the response reports role=ADMIN.
  - SeedTokenCacheForTest and PeekTokenCache test seams are
    exported so handlers_test package can drive the in-memory
    cache directly.

fix(auth): wire JWT revocation — logout route + invalidate on delete/demote/password

Token revocation was an open gap: a deleted or demoted user's JWT stayed valid
for up to 24h, and there was no logout.

- middleware/auth.js: add an in-memory token denylist + per-user invalidation
  cutoff. authenticate() now rejects logged-out tokens and any token whose `iat`
  predates the user's invalidation (delete / role / school / password change).
  Sets req.token; exports logoutToken + invalidateUser.
- server.js: add POST /api/auth/logout (revoke presented token); invalidate the
  user on change-password, on DELETE /api/admins/:id, and on PUT /api/admins/:id
  when role/schoolId/password change.
- change-password now ends all sessions for the user (secure default) — parent
  doc updated to send the user back to login afterward; logout documented too.
- tests: logout succeeds and the reused token is rejected (401 revoked). 36 pass.

Note: revocation state is in-memory (resets on restart, per-instance). For
multi-instance / restart-safe revocation, back it with Redis or a tokenVersion
column.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Invalidate refresh tokens on role or manager_id change

Invalidate all refresh tokens when role or manager_id changes to prevent stale role usage.

fix(security): invalidate tokens on admin/role privilege change (Closes #1821) (#1827)

* fix(security): invalidate tokens on admin/role privilege change (Closes #1821)

Admin demotion (is_admin true->false) and SSO role-set re-sync only bumped
updated_at, which is deliberately excluded from the credential-change
watermark (#1190). Because is_admin is baked into JWT claims at mint time
with no DB recheck, a demoted admin kept admin authority until token expiry.

Add a dedicated privileges_changed_at column, fold it into
fetch_credential_change_watermark's GREATEST(), and bump it on actual
privilege changes in update_user and apply_role_mapping (skipping no-op
re-applies so benign profile edits stay non-invalidating). Also fires the
in-memory invalidate_user_tokens fast-path for same-replica immediacy.

* chore(migrations): renumber 130_users_privileges_changed_at.sql -> 131_users_privileges_changed_at.sql to avoid 130 collision with #1810/sibling PRs

feat(auth): role cache invalidation via perm_version

- migration: DB trigger auto-bumps users.perm_version on user_roles
  INSERT/DELETE, so role edits take effect on next request
- middleware/authn: AuthN now accepts pool and validates perm_version
  against DB each request; mismatch returns 401 PERM_VERSION_CHANGED
  so frontend auto-refreshes to pick up latest permissions
- middleware/rbac: cache key includes perm_version for auto-invalidation
  when roles change (no stale 5m TTL on revoked permissions)
- router: pass pool to AuthN middleware in both auth and authenticated groups

Flow: admin changes role -> trigger bumps perm_version -> next request
returns 401 PERM_VERSION_CHANGED -> client auto-refresh -> retry with
new token -> role check uses fresh data.

Refs: PRD v3.1 FR-AUTH-08, NFR-SEC RBAC real-time invalidation

commit.message:
fix(rbac): stop caching the API authorization decision

Invalidating the token cache across processes fixed the lost wakeup but left the
authorization decision itself cached under a TTL equal to the token lifetime, so any
invalidation that failed to reach a process was an authentication bypass for the whole
remaining life of the token.

Take the decision out of the cache instead. check_token now re-reads the account, its
roles and the token blacklist on every request, and only optimize_resources -- the
expensive half, a pure function of the roles -- stays cached, keyed on the roles alone.
A cache hit can no longer authenticate a deleted, blacklisted or re-roled user, so no
signal has to arrive for a revocation to take effect.

The cache TTL no longer derives from auth_token_exp_timeout. Tying it to the token
lifetime guaranteed a missed invalidation was never recovered from before the token died
anyway; a short fixed TTL bounds the staleness of the policies it now holds. This also
drops the api.configuration import from the framework package.

generate_keypair loses its functools.cache, which change_keypair cleared only in the
process that handled the revocation. It is now stamped with the key files' identity, so
every process picks up a rotation on its own next call rather than depending on the
inotify watcher in api.signals, which only runs in the API's main process.

TokenManager.delete_all_rules also invalidates now. It is the revoke_tokens path and,
through it, rbac_db_factory_reset, which recreates the RBAC database from scratch: the
policies cached for a set of roles no longer describe what those roles grant.

commit.message:
docs: embed effective roles in access-token claims, revoke via token_version

Reverse the earlier decision to always re-resolve RoleAssignment/team
membership from the DB per request. Access tokens now carry a roles
claim (flattened snapshot of direct + team-inherited grants) and a tv
claim (User.token_version at issuance), closer to how Keycloak embeds
roles. Authorization middleware reads roles straight from the token
instead of joining role_assignments/team_members/teams on every
request; a single indexed point-lookup on token_version still gives
immediate revocation (token_version is bumped, individually or
cascaded to a team's current members, on any RoleAssignment/team
membership change, deactivation, or password change). Both grant
types on POST /v1/auth/token always recompute roles/tv fresh so a
refresh after invalidation reflects current permissions. Adds
users.token_version to log-server-storage and updates
log-server-auth/log-server-rbac accordingly.

commit.message:
Strengthen session handling and login token security (#327)

This change strengthens how the app handles login sessions and access tokens.

What changed:

- Access tokens and refresh tokens now follow a single, versioned validation path. A refresh token can no longer be presented in place of an access token, and both must carry the expected session information to be accepted.
- Server-side authorization now reads the user's current role and company membership from the database on every request rather than trusting the values embedded in a token. Role and membership changes take effect immediately.
- Sessions are invalidated consistently on logout, password change, and password reset, and when an administrator changes a user's security fields. Previously issued tokens stop working right away.
- The live event stream fully validates its bearer token before the stream is opened.
- When a token is rejected, stale session cookies are cleared so the browser returns to a clean signed-out state.

Existing behavior for normal sign-in, refresh, and the event stream is preserved. The change adds a regression suite covering the token contract, session invalidation triggers, and the event-stream checks.

commit.message:
fix(security): invalidate tokens + clear stale grade_scope on admin role/scope change

PUT /api/admin/users/:id changed role/scope_type/scope_id but did not invalidate
the user's existing tokens, so a demoted/rescoped account kept its old elevated
role + scope until the access token expired (up to 24h) and could even refresh
into a new access token still carrying the stale role (auth.js and /refresh-token
read role/scope from the token).

L1 — when role OR scope actually changes, also set password_changed_at = NOW() in
the same UPDATE; the existing iat<password_changed_at guard in auth.js and
/refresh-token then forces a re-login under the new role/scope. The bump only
fires on a real change (re-saving the same role/scope, or editing only
display_name/is_active, does not log the user out).

L6 — when the new role is not 'school', clear grade_scope (= NULL) so a stale
grade-band scope can't linger after a role change (the create path already
rejects grade_scope for non-school roles).

Both fold into the single existing UPDATE — zero new query, no hot-path change.

Security audit 2026-06-27 (LOW L1 + L6).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Add JWT token version revocation support

Implement server-side JWT invalidation using a new `users.token_version` column (Flyway V14) and propagate it through user models, mappers, principals, and token claims. The auth filter now cross-checks token claims against current DB state (active status, token version, and role consistency) so deactivated users, stale tokens, and role-contradicting tokens are rejected. Adds `/api/auth/logout` to revoke active sessions, increments token version on deactivation/provisioning/role updates, records new audit events for token revocation and role changes, updates seed data, and expands security tests to cover these revocation and authorization scenarios.

commit.message:
Sign out every device on password, role, permission or access change

A password change/reset, role change, permission-override change, branch
access change, or deactivation now ends every session the user has:

- SessionRevocationService rotates the SecurityStamp, revokes all refresh
  tokens, invalidates the permission and stamp caches, and pushes
  SessionRevoked to the user's SignalR connections.
- Access tokens carry an "sstamp" claim; JwtBearer OnTokenValidated rejects
  a token whose stamp no longer matches (or a banned/deleted user) via a
  cached lookup, so an already-issued token stops working immediately.
- Wired into ChangePassword, ResetPassword, AdminResetUserPassword,
  AssignRolesToUser, UpdateUserPermissions, UpdateUserBranches,
  ToggleUserActive (on deactivate) and BanOwner. Role/permission/branch
  saves only revoke when the set actually changed.
- ResetPassword now runs its password write under the user's own tenant;
  the anonymous request has no ambient tenant for the write guard.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01TsGFatXtZ7VW2DubkUymPT

fix(identity): gate self-registration, per-session refresh with grace, revoke on password change

Self-registration (finding 1)
- /identity/self-register is OFF by default and per-tenant opt-in via
  SelfRegistration:AllowedTenants (never root); disabled tenants get 404.
- New SelfRegisterUserCommand (no branch selection) creates the user
  UNCONFIRMED with the Basic role and emails a confirmation link. Admin
  creation (/identity/register) is unchanged.

Permissions (findings 5, 15)
- UserPermissionService never keeps an empty permission set in cache, keys
  entries by tenant (caller's own tenant claim for the signed-in user) and
  tags them per user; invalidation clears every variant.
- IdentityDbInitializer and default-role assignment check the
  AddToRoleAsync result; the seeded admin's permission cache is invalidated
  after the role is assigned (flaky 403 in CI).
- RequiredPermissionAuthorizationHandler requires ALL declared permissions.

Sessions (findings 6, 10, 14, 4)
- Refresh tokens are validated per session (UserSession) when the per-user
  column does not match, so a second device signing in no longer logs the
  first out; the just-rotated token stays valid for 30s
  (RefreshTokenReuseGrace) to absorb concurrent refreshes.
  Migration: UserSessions.PreviousRefreshTokenHash + RefreshTokenRotatedAt.
- New anonymous POST /identity/token/revoke (sign-out, idempotent, 204).
- Password reset/change clear the stored refresh token and revoke all
  sessions; reset also updates password history and expiry.
- Token refresh is no longer on the strict "auth" rate-limit policy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Harden authentication: token rotation, revocation and lock-out

- refresh tokens stored server-side and rotated; replaying an old one revokes the session
- /auth/logout and /auth/logout-all; password/role changes invalidate existing tokens
- login lock-out per email and IP; constant-time check for unknown emails
- python-jose (unmaintained) replaced by PyJWT with iss/iat/nbf/jti checks
- passlib replaced by bcrypt with SHA-256 pre-hash (no 72-byte truncation)
- SECRET_KEY required in production (a random default broke tokens on restart)
- malformed token subjects / user IDs return 401/422 instead of 500
- new-password strength validated; admin search, activate, role change, self-lockout guards
- database-agnostic UUID type, Alembic migrations, create_admin script
- security headers, CORS config, pytest suite on SQLite

feat(server): invalidate dashboard tokens on privilege changes

JWTs carried no revocation handle: changing a password or demoting or
disabling an account left every previously issued token valid until
expiry. Access and refresh tokens now embed the account's
token_version, and the AuthUser extractor and the refresh endpoint
refuse mismatches.

change) and on role changes or disabling from user management. Tokens
minted before the claim existed deserialize as version 0, so upgrading
does not log anyone out — every later bump takes effect immediately.

commit.message:
G0.9 (TR-04): prove SEC-05 for role removal

SEC-05 covers two things: deactivating a user, *or* removing their
role, invalidates an issued token. Only deactivation was tested. Role
removal is a different code path - the token carries a role that
deps.get_principal must re-validate against the user's current roles on
every request - and an `active`-only check would pass the existing test
while leaving a revoked role usable.

- `test_sec_05_removing_a_role_invalidates_a_token_for_that_role`: the
  user stays active, so the refusal can only come from the role check.
  Asserts 403 with the message naming the role, that the user is still
  active, and that they can sign in again under the role they now hold.
- `test_sec_05_removing_one_role_leaves_tokens_for_the_others`: U-040
  holds MRC Member and Executive; removing one refuses that token and
  leaves the other working. Added beyond the finding, because a
  per-*user* invalidation would pass the single-role test and still be
  wrong.

Roles are changed through `user_service.upsert_user`, the path a T01
re-import uses, rather than by deleting user_role rows - the test
drives production code instead of reaching around it. There is still no
API to change roles or deactivate a user (CR-19), so both tests call
the service directly, as the existing deactivation test does.

Verified against a defect that trusts the role claim in the token: both
new tests fail with 200 where 403 is required, while the deactivation
test still passes - confirming they cover ground it did not.

Suite 157 / 153 pass; PostgreSQL 4 / 4. All four High test gaps from
the first review are now closed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
feat(api): admin profile + change-password endpoints

GET  /api/admin/profile        → id/name/email/phone/avatar_url/role
POST /api/admin/change-password → verifies the current password, rejects
                                  reusing it, then invalidates EVERY token

Why a separate endpoint instead of reusing the pharmacy flow: the pharmacy
change-password route begins with `abort_unless($user->role === 'pharmacy',
403)` — it refuses an admin by design. Relaxing that to share one route would
have opened pharmacy password changes to an admin path, so the hardened rules
are duplicated inside their own role scope instead.

`avatar_url` is resolved with `Image::url`, same as the medicine image: the
stored column is a Cloudinary value a client cannot load directly.

The endpoint sits behind the existing `auth:sanctum` + `role:admin` group and
is throttled (6/min) — a password form is the one place a stolen session can be
escalated into a permanent takeover.

Tests: 5 cases (avatar_url not the raw path, wrong current password, same
password reuse, token invalidation on success, short password). All pass.

commit.message:
feat(BOU-191): rotate sessions on password + role change (#281)

* feat(security): rotate sessions on password + role change (BOU-191)

Session-management defense-in-depth gap: a password change left older sessions
authenticated, and a role change let a live session retain its old privileges
(invalidate-all-user-sessions was only wired into logout-user-everywhere).

Wire session invalidation into the user service:
- change-password -> invalidate ALL of the user's sessions (a credential change
  forces re-authentication everywhere with the new password).
- update-user-profile -> when :role changes, invalidate the user's sessions so a
  demotion cannot retain elevated access and a promotion starts a fresh session.
  An ordinary (non-role) profile edit does not churn sessions.

Login-time invalidation is intentionally NOT added: multi-device use is
legitimate and session fixation is already prevented by the SecureRandom,
server-minted token (see BOU-168).

Adds a ^:security test asserting invalidation fires on password + role change
and does not fire on a plain profile update; fixes change-password-test's
session-repo stub (previously nil).

Refs BOU-191

* chore(lint): localized ignore for partial session-repo reify in service_test

* fix(security): guard role-change invalidation against partial updates (review)

Only invalidate on role change when the updated entity actually carries :role,
so a future partial update that omits :role is not misread as a demotion and
does not churn the user's sessions. No behaviour change for current callers
(all pass full merged entities).

commit.message:
fix(auth): invalidate sessions on password change, account disable, and role change (#217)

Live sessions were not invalidated by security-relevant account changes, and
admin capabilities were frozen for the lifetime of the refresh token:

- Password change, disabling/deleting a mailbox or admin, and changing an
  admin's roles had no effect on existing sessions until the refresh token
  expired (default 7 days).
- Refresh re-minted token pairs purely from the refresh-token claims: it never
  reloaded the account, so it did not re-check whether the account was still
  active and copied an admin's capabilities from the up-to-7-day-old token
  rather than re-deriving them from the database.

Fix:

- Refresh now re-reads live account state before issuing new tokens. It refuses
  a disabled or deleted account (and revokes that owner's remaining sessions),
  and re-derives an admin's capabilities from the current roles instead of
  trusting the token claim. When the backing store is unreachable it fails
  closed, consistent with the existing rotation-ledger check. A nil store
  (DB-less unit tests) preserves the prior claim-based behaviour, so the
  session-type-preservation guarantee across refresh is unchanged.
- Mailbox and admin handlers revoke every session for the owner on password
  change, on active transitioning to false, on admin role changes, and on
  delete.

Tests (red-green, DB-backed):

- Refresh is rejected after a mailbox/admin is disabled.
- A demoted admin's refreshed access token carries the reduced, DB-derived
  capability set, not the stale token claim.
- Password change, disable, role change, and delete each revoke the owner's
  refresh tokens (mailbox and admin).
- Existing rotation, revocation, logout, and session-type-preservation tests
  continue to pass.

Closes #164

  periodic refresh

fix(auth): keep devices signed in when their role is promoted

SetRole revoked the target's refresh family and closed its live socket on any role change, so promoting a device (device -> admin) logged it out. Split the change by privilege: promotions keep the session and only invalidate the access token so the next request re-issues one with the new scopes; demotions still revoke the refresh family, reject issued access tokens and close sockets so reduced privileges take effect immediately. Adds role-rank classification, a promotion regression test, and updates the README.

commit.message:
test(#267): lock §8.1.6 role-change invalidation as satisfied-by-architecture

Arc E first wave's §8.1.6 verification gate — "a role change mid-session
takes effect immediately on the next request without operator action" — is
already met, by a mechanism better than the one the design described.

The design assumed roles live in the session token, so it specified a
401 token-stale -> refresh-required -> transparent-refresh dance to pick up
new claims after a role change. Aurora-Locus never embeds the role:
finalize_admin_role resolves it live from admin_role_manager.get_role(did)
on every request, across all three auth layers (local session, HS256 admin
JWT, ES256K service-auth). The token carries only `scope`, never the tier.
So there is no stale claim to invalidate — elevation, downgrade, and full
revocation all take effect on the operator's very next request for free.

This adds the gate-locking test: it mints ONE admin token, then asserts the
same token reflects a revoke+re-grant (Moderator -> Admin) and then a full
revoke (-> 403 Authorization) on the immediately following
admin_auth_from_token call, with no re-mint. Building the design's literal
token-stale machinery was declined as a deliberate decision — it would be a
refresh round-trip with zero behavioral change. The design->implementation
translation is recorded in the §8.1.6 doc note (untracked internal design).

§8.1.7 SuperAdmin force-logout (0.9.3) is a separate capability — it
invalidates sessions, not role claims — and is unaffected.

Close-gate: clippy clean, full lib suite 1381/0.

Refs #267.

feat: session invalidation on password reset / role change (JFR-94)

Adds a per-user sessionVersion counter (schema + migration). The jwt callback
fetches the current DB version on every auth() call and marks the token
invalidated when the version doesn't match. getCurrentUser() and requireAdmin()
treat invalidated tokens as logged-out, so existing if-no-user patterns across
the app need no changes.

sessionVersion is incremented by adminResetUserPassword, adminUpdateUser (role
change only), and changePassword (self-service). Self-service password change
also calls session.update() from the client to re-arm the active session, so
only other sessions/devices are logged out. Converted changePassword() throws
to the ActionResult pattern to avoid Next.js production message redaction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(auth): email/password login with revocable JWTs

Login now takes email+password and delegates to the accounts
context's AuthenticateAccountPort instead of comparing against
a single shared configured password. JWTs carry the real
account id, role, and a token_version claim; JwtAuthFilter
re-checks the account on every request via AccountQueryPort so
a disabled account, role change, or version bump (password
change, admin reset, logout-all) invalidates already-issued
tokens instead of waiting out their expiry.

fix: address lint findings in new code

- Handle errors on post-reset/email-change token invalidation (log

- Check the role type assertion in assignableOrgRoles.
